explanations.detail: Human ability-bonus selection (choice:human_ability_bonus -> ability:intelligence) applies the PF1 Core Rulebook Standard Human +2 racial bonus to intelligence BEFORE ability modifiers are derived: base chosen score 16 + 2 racial = 18. This differs from Dwarf/Half-Elf/etc., whose fixtures pre-bake their own racial adjustment into the chosen score itself (no arithmetic performed on those seams); Human's chosen score is confirmed PRE-bonus by both the deterministic pilot fixture and the real PCGen oracle output.
strength ability modifier from chosen score 8: floor(8 / 2) - 5 = -1
dexterity ability modifier from chosen score 14: floor(14 / 2) - 5 = 2
constitution ability modifier from chosen score 13: floor(13 / 2) - 5 = 1
intelligence ability modifier from chosen score 18: floor(18 / 2) - 5 = 4
wisdom ability modifier from chosen score 12: floor(12 / 2) - 5 = 1
charisma ability modifier from chosen score 10: floor(10 / 2) - 5 = 0

Baseline melee attack bonus for the Longsword: Wizard base attack bonus (+2) + Strength modifier (+-1) + Weapon Focus (Longsword) (+1) + Medium size modifier (+0, PF1 Table 8-1 -- attack rolls take the same size modifier as Armor Class) -4 nonproficiency penalty (this class has no Longsword proficiency in the corpus); Power Attack is selected but inactive (+0) = -2

Baseline armor class: base 10 + Chain Shirt armor bonus (+4) + Dexterity contribution (+2, DEX modifier +2 within MAXDEX:4) + Medium size modifier (+0, PF1 Table 8-1) + Dodge (+1, only for a character actually carrying feat:dodge) + Barbarian Rage penalty (0, only while actively, validly raging) + Skald Inspired Rage penalty (0, only while actively, validly singing) + Bloodrager Bloodrage penalty (0, only while actively, validly bloodraging) + Brawler AC Bonus (+0, while wearing light or no armor) + Alchemist Mutagen natural armor bonus (+0, only while actively, validly mutated) + Inquisitor Protection judgment sacred/profane bonus (+0, only while actively, validly judging Protection) + Oracle Nature's Whispers Charisma-for-Dexterity substitution (+0, only for a Nature-Mystery Oracle who took that revelation) + Cavalier Challenge penalty (0, only while actively challenging) + Sorcerer Draconic Bloodline Dragon Resistances natural armor bonus (+0, only for a Draconic-bloodline Sorcerer at 3rd level or higher) + ARG Armor of the Pit natural armor bonus (+0, only for a character holding that feat who did NOT take the Scaled Skin alternate racial trait); shield is absent (+0) = 17

Touch armor class: the armor class above (17) with the contributors a touch attack ignores removed -- Chain Shirt armor bonus (-4), Alchemist Mutagen natural armor (-0), Sorcerer Draconic Bloodline natural armor (-0), ARG Armor of the Pit natural armor (-0); shield is absent (-0). The Dexterity contribution (+2), the Medium size modifier (+0, PF1 Table 8-1) and every dodge/sacred/ability bonus and penalty are all retained = 13

Flat-footed armor class: the armor class above (17) with the contributors a flat-footed character is denied removed -- the Dexterity contribution (-2, bonus only; a Dexterity penalty is kept) including the Oracle Nature's Whispers Charisma-for-Dexterity substitution (-0, which stands in for that bonus), and every dodge-typed bonus (-1: Dodge's +1, per PF1 "any situation that denies you your Dexterity bonus to Armor Class also denies you dodge bonuses"). The Chain Shirt armor bonus (+4), the Medium size modifier (+0), every natural armor and sacred/profane bonus, every penalty, and Brawler's AC Bonus (+0, whose own rule text applies it even when flat-footed) are all retained = 14

Combat Maneuver Bonus: Wizard base attack bonus (+2) + Strength modifier (+-1) + Medium special size modifier (+0) = 1. The special size modifier runs OPPOSITE to Table 8-1's Armor Class column: being smaller makes a creature worse at combat maneuvers, not better. No Improved/Greater maneuver feat or size-changing effect is modelled by this engine, so none is summed here

Combat Maneuver Defense: base 10 + Wizard base attack bonus (+2) + Strength modifier (+-1) + Dexterity modifier (+2) + Medium special size modifier (+0) = 13. These are exactly the terms PF1's published CMD formula prints; the deflection/dodge/insight/luck/morale/profane/sacred bonuses to Armor Class that also apply to CMD in real PF1 are NOT folded in here yet, and are named rather than silently implied

Attack bonus with the equipped Longsword: base attack bonus (+2) + governing ability modifier (-1) + weapon feats (+1) + nonproficiency penalty (-4) + size modifier (+0) = -2. Weapon Focus / Greater Weapon Focus name this weapon, adding +1 to the attack roll. -4 nonproficiency penalty: nothing this character holds grants proficiency with this weapon -- neither a class grant nor Simple/Martial/Exotic Weapon Proficiency naming it. Only the Focus feats reach this total -- the Specialization feats are damage and Improved Critical is threat range, both grounded separately. Separate from combat.baseline_melee_attack_bonus, which stays a Longsword-specific GE-06 fixture total until task #80 generalises it

Feat damage bonus with the equipped Longsword: +0. No Weapon Specialization or Greater Weapon Specialization names this weapon, so no feat bonus applies to its damage rolls. This is the feat contribution alone, NOT a damage total: the weapon's own 1d8 damage die and the Strength-to-damage contribution are excluded, because Strength applies at 1x one-handed, 1.5x two-handed and 0.5x off-hand and this engine does not record how a weapon is being wielded

Critical threat range with the equipped Longsword: 19-20/x2. Improved Critical does not name this weapon, so its threat range is the weapon's printed one. The value grounded here is the LOW end of the range; the corpus stores CRITRANGE as a width, so the range is 21-width..=20

Total Fortitude save: Wizard base Fortitude save (+1) + Constitution modifier (+1) + feat bonus (+0, Great Fortitude if selected) + Good domain Touch of Good sacred bonus (+0, self-applied) + Inquisitor Purity judgment sacred/profane bonus (+0, only while actively, validly judging Purity) + alternate racial trait (+0, only for a character who took one that declares a Fortitude bonus) + character trait (+0, Life of Toil if selected) = 2

Total Reflex save: Wizard base Reflex save (+1) + Dexterity modifier (+2) + feat bonus (+0, Lightning Reflexes if selected) + Good domain Touch of Good sacred bonus (+0, self-applied) + Inquisitor Purity judgment sacred/profane bonus (+0, only while actively, validly judging Purity) + Oracle Sidestep Secret Charisma-for-Dexterity substitution (+0, only for a Lore-Mystery Oracle who took that revelation) + alternate racial trait (+0, only for a character who took one that declares a Reflex modifier -- this one can be NEGATIVE, e.g. Horror Adventures' Half-Elf Mismatched at -2) + character trait (+0, no ultimate_campaign trait currently declares a Reflex bonus, so always 0) = 3

Total Will save: Wizard base Will save (+4) + Wisdom modifier (+1) + feat bonus (+0, Iron Will if selected) + Barbarian Rage morale bonus (+0, only while actively, validly raging) + Skald Inspired Rage morale bonus (+0, only while actively, validly singing) + Bloodrager Bloodrage morale bonus (+0, only while actively, validly bloodraging) + Good domain Touch of Good sacred bonus (+0, self-applied) + Inquisitor Purity judgment sacred/profane bonus (+0, only while actively, validly judging Purity) + alternate racial trait (+0, only for a character who took one that declares a Will bonus -- ARG p.42's Half-Elf Dual Minded is the one such trait in the corpus today) + character trait (+0, Indomitable Faith if selected) = 5

Selected Climb modifier: rank 1 + Strength modifier (-1) + no class-skill bonus (Climb is not a class skill for this character's class) + Chain Shirt armor-check penalty (-2) + feat bonus (+0, Athletic if selected) = -2

Selected Intimidate modifier: rank 1 + Charisma modifier (+0) + no class-skill bonus (Intimidate is not a class skill for this character's class) + feat bonus (+0, Persuasive and/or Intimidating Prowess if selected) = 1

Selected Swim modifier: rank 1 + Strength modifier (-1) + no class-skill bonus (Swim is not a class skill for this character's class) + Chain Shirt armor-check penalty (-2) + feat bonus (+0, Athletic if selected) + Witch Flight hex (+0) = -2

Weapon Focus (longsword) grants a +1 bonus on attack rolls with that weapon (+2 when Greater Weapon Focus names it too). This bonus is also carried inside combat.weapon_attack_bonus.<weapon> whenever that weapon is equipped; this record is the component fact, that one is the total, and the two agreeing is expected rather than a double-count. It still grounds standalone, because the feat's bonus is real whether or not the chosen weapon happens to be equipped. Requires an explicit recorded weapon choice -- nothing is seeded, per the same no-silent-seeding design as Skill Focus

Wizard Weapon and Armor Proficiency (corpus KEY:Wizard ~ Weapon and Armor Proficiency): "Wizards are proficient with the club, dagger, heavy crossbow, light crossbow, and quarterstaff, but not with any type of armor or shield. The weapon half's real mechanical consequence -- avoiding the -4 nonproficiency attack penalty -- is already grounded separately by `weapon_tables::class_weapon_proficiency("class:wizard")`, which this record does not duplicate. No armor-nonproficiency-penalty mechanic exists anywhere in this engine

Recognized Wizard level 5 Scribe Scroll bonus feat grant: every Wizard, regardless of arcane school specialization, is granted Scribe Scroll as a bonus feat at 1st level (PF1 Core Rulebook Wizard class feature), letting the Wizard create scrolls of spells they know. This is a one-time grant recognized once and kept thereafter, not re-granted at 2nd level or later. This is a bounded grant-only recognition: it carries no fabricated mechanical value (+0) and computes no scroll creation cost, no crafting time, no spellbook content, and no spell-slot machinery

Recognized Wizard level 5 school specialization choice: the canonical deterministic selections choose Evocation as the specialty arcane school (choice:wizard_school_specialization -> school:evocation) with Necromancy and Transmutation as the two opposed schools (choice:wizard_opposed_schools -> school:necromancy, school:transmutation), per the PF1 Core Rulebook arcane school class feature. A wizard's chosen school does not change by level, so this recognition is not level-gated. This is a bounded recognition record of the choice identity only: it carries no fabricated mechanical value (+0) and computes no school power, no opposed-school preparation cost, and no spell math

Wizard level 5 specialist bonus spell slot: a specialist wizard gains one additional Evocation-only spell slot of each spell level she can cast, 1st and up, usable only for spells of the chosen school (PF1 Core Rulebook arcane school class feature). At levels 1-2 a wizard casts only 1st-level spells, so the flat count is exactly one 1st-level Evocation-only bonus slot (+1); at level 3+ a wizard also casts 2nd-level spells for the first time (verified against both primary sources' raw spells-per-day table rows), so the flat count becomes +2 (one 1st-level Evocation-only bonus slot plus one 2nd-level Evocation-only bonus slot); at level 5+ a wizard also casts 3rd-level spells for the first time (verified against both primary sources' raw spells-per-day table rows), so the flat count becomes +3 (one 1st-level, one 2nd-level, and one 3rd-level Evocation-only bonus slot); at level 7+ a wizard also casts 4th-level spells for the first time (verified against both primary sources' raw spells-per-day table rows), so the flat count becomes +4 (one 1st-level, one 2nd-level, one 3rd-level, and one 4th-level Evocation-only bonus slot); at level 9+ a wizard also casts 5th-level spells for the first time (verified against both primary sources' raw spells-per-day table rows), so the flat count becomes +5; at level 11+ a wizard also casts 6th-level spells for the first time (verified independently against both primary sources' raw spells-per-day table rows: the level-10 row is "4/4/4/3/3/2" with a still-"—" 6th-level column, the level-11 row is "4/4/4/4/3/2/1", the first non-"—" 6th-level column), so the flat count becomes +6 (one bonus slot of each spell level 1st through 6th); at level 13+ a wizard also casts 7th-level spells for the first time (verified independently against both primary sources' raw spells-per-day table rows: the level-12 row is "4/4/4/4/3/3/2" with a still-"—" 7th-level column, the level-13 row is "4/4/4/4/4/3/2/1", the first non-"—" 7th-level column), so the flat count becomes +7 (one bonus slot of each spell level 1st through 7th); at level 15+ a wizard also casts 8th-level spells for the first time (verified independently against both primary sources' raw spells-per-day table rows: the level-14 row is "4/4/4/4/4/3/3/2" with a still-"—" 8th-level column, the level-15 row is "4/4/4/4/4/4/3/2/1", the first non-"—" 8th-level column), so the flat count becomes +8 (one bonus slot of each spell level 1st through 8th); at level 17+ a wizard also casts 9th-level spells for the first time (verified independently against both primary sources' raw spells-per-day table rows: the level-16 row is "4/4/4/4/4/4/3/3/2" with a still-"—" 9th-level column, the level-17 row is "4/4/4/4/4/4/4/3/2/1", the first non-"—" 9th-level column), so the flat count becomes +9 (one bonus slot of each spell level 1st through 9th). At level 5 this is +3 flat count; there is no cantrip-level bonus slot. This grounds the flat count only: no slot contents, no spells prepared per day, no per-day slot totals, and no bonus slots from a high Intelligence are computed

At Wizard level 5 this is max(5 / 2, 1) = 2. This grounds only the flat bonus-damage magnitude; it applies no bonus to any actual spell-damage roll and implements no spell-damage-application engine

Wizard caster level at Wizard level 5: 5, transcribed from the book's own caster-level rule (core_rulebook/cr_classes.lst:281). The book's rule routes the caster level through an intermediate variable that resolves to the class level: the two terms that could raise it are both 0 for a base-class character — one is raised only by opt-in item and trait content, the other only by bloodline and archetype records. The rule carries no level gate, so it applies from class level 1. The class's declared spellcasting ability (INT) is named for reference only. This grounds the caster level and nothing else: no spells known, no spells per day, no bonus spell slots from a high INT, no spell save DC, and no per-spell dice counts are computed from it. The Spells tab already renders each spell's own description text, which is where a "per caster level" scaling clause and its cap live

sheetLines.label: Wizard
sheetLines.prose:
Hit die: d6
Skill ranks per level: 2

sheetLines.label: Arcane Bond
sheetLines.prose: At 1st level, wizards form a powerful bond with an object or a creature. This bond can take one of two forms: a familiar or a bonded object. A familiar is a magical pet that enhances the wizard's skills and senses and can aid him in magic, while a bonded object is an item a wizard can use to cast additional spells or to serve as a magical item. Once a wizard makes this choice, it is permanent and cannot be changed.

sheetLines.label: Arcane School
sheetLines.prose:
A wizard can choose to specialize in one school of magic, gaining additional spells and powers based on that school. This choice must be made at 1st level, and once made, it cannot be changed. A wizard that does not select a school receives the universalist school instead.
A wizard that chooses to specialize in one school of magic must select two other schools as his opposition schools, representing knowledge sacrificed in one area of arcane lore to gain mastery in another. A wizard who prepares spells from his opposition schools must use two spell slots of that level to prepare the spell. In addition, a specialist takes a -4 penalty on any skill checks made when crafting a magic item that has a spell from one of his opposition schools as a prerequisite. A universalist wizard can prepare spells from any school without restriction.
Each arcane school gives the wizard a number of school powers. In addition, specialist wizards receive an additional spell slot of each spell level he can cast, from 1st on up. Each day, a wizard can prepare a spell from his specialty school in that slot. This spell must be in the wizard's spellbook. A wizard can select a spell modified by a metamagic feat to prepare in his school slot, but it uses up a higher-level spell slot. Wizards with the universalist school do not receive a school slot.

sheetLines.label: Cantrips
sheetLines.prose: Wizards can prepare a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, each day. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they are not expended when cast and may be used again. A wizard can prepare a cantrip from an opposed school, but it uses up two of his available slots.

sheetLines.label: Spells
sheetLines.prose:
A wizard casts arcane spells drawn from the sorcerer/wizard spell list presented in Chapter 10. A wizard must choose and prepare his spells ahead of time.
To learn, prepare, or cast a spell, the wizard must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a wizard's spell is 10 + the spell level + the wizard's Intelligence modifier.
A wizard can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. His base daily spell allotment is given on Table 3-16. In addition, he receives bonus spells per day if he has a high Intelligence score (see Table 1-3).
A wizard may know any number of spells. He must choose and prepare his spells ahead of time by getting 8 hours of sleep and spending 1 hour studying his spellbook. While studying, the wizard decides which spells to prepare.

sheetLines.label: Chain Shirt
sheetLines.prose:
Covering the torso, this shirt is made up of thousands of interlocking metal rings.
Armor check penalty: -2
Max Dex bonus: 4
Arcane spell failure: 20%

sheetLines.label: Longsword
sheetLines.prose:
This sword is about 3-1/2 feet in length.
Critical multiplier: x2
Critical threat: 19-20

sheetLines.label: Dodge
sheetLines.prose:
Your training and reflexes allow you to react swiftly to avoid an opponent's attack.
You gain a +1 dodge bonus to your AC. A condition that makes you lose your Dex bonus to AC also makes you lose the benefits of this feat.

sheetLines.label: Power Attack
sheetLines.prose:
You can make exceptionally deadly melee attacks by sacrificing accuracy for strength.
You can choose to take a -1 penalty on all melee attack rolls and combat maneuver checks to gain a +2 bonus on all melee damage rolls. This bonus to damage is increased by half (+50%) if you are making an attack with a two-handed weapon, a one handed weapon using two hands, or a primary natural weapon that adds 1-1/2 times your Strength modifier on damage rolls. This bonus to damage is halved (-50%) if you are making an attack with an off-hand weapon or secondary natural weapon. You must choose to use this feat before making an attack roll, and its effects last until your next turn. The bonus damage does not apply to touch attacks or effects that do not deal hit point damage.

sheetLines.label: Weapon Focus
sheetLines.prose:
You are especially good at using your chosen weapon.
You gain a +1 bonus on all attack rolls you make using the selected weapon.

sheetLines.label: Fireball
sheetLines.prose:
A fireball spell generates a searing explosion of flame that detonates with a low roar and deals 1d6 points of fire damage per caster level (maximum 10d6) to every creature within the area. Unattended objects also take this damage. The explosion creates almost no pressure. You point your finger and determine the range (distance and height) at which the fireball is to burst. A glowing, pea-sized bead streaks from the pointing digit and, unless it impacts upon a material body or solid barrier prior to attaining the prescribed range, blossoms into the fireball at that point. An early impact results in an early detonation. If you attempt to send the bead through a narrow passage, such as through an arrow slit, you must "hit" the opening with a ranged touch attack, or else the bead strikes the barrier and detonates prematurely. The fireball sets fire to combustibles and damages objects in the area. It can melt metals with low melting points, such as lead, gold, copper, silver, and bronze. If the damage caused to an interposing barrier shatters or breaks through it, the fireball may continue beyond the barrier if the area permits; otherwise it stops at the barrier just as any other spell effect does.
Casting time: 1 standard action
Components: V, S, M
Descriptor: Fire
Duration: Instantaneous
Range: 400 ft.
Saving throw: Reflex half
School: Evocation
Spell resistance: Yes
Target or area: 20-ft.-radius spread
School: FireSchool

sheetLines.label: Light
sheetLines.prose:
This spell causes a touched object to glow like a torch, shedding normal light in a 20-foot radius, and increasing the light level for an additional 20 feet by one step, up to normal light (darkness becomes dim light, and dim light becomes normal light). In an area of normal or bright light, this spell has no effect. The effect is immobile, but it can be cast on a movable object. You can only have one light spell active at any one time. If you cast this spell while another casting is still in effect, the previous casting is dispelled. If you make this spell permanent (through permanency or a similar effect), it does not count against this limit. Light can be used to counter or dispel any darkness spell of equal or lower spell level.
Casting time: 1 standard action
Components: V, M/DF
Descriptor: Light
Duration: 0 minutes
Range: Touch
Saving throw: None
School: Evocation
Spell resistance: No
Target or area: Object touched
Descriptor: WoodSchool
